questions.q: Calculate the molality of KI if the density of 20% (mass/mass) aqueous KI is 1.202 gmL<sup>-1</sup>. Report your final answer by rounding off the molality correct upto one place of decimal and then multiplying it by 10.

Weight of KI in 100g of water = 20 g

Weight of water in the solution = 100 - 20 = 80 g= 0.08 kg

Molar mass of KI = 39 + 127 = 166 g mol-1

$\text{Molality of the solution (m)} = \dfrac{\text{Number of moles of KI}}{\text{Mass of water in kg}}$

$= \dfrac{\left(2 0 \text{g}\right) / \left(1 6 6 \text{g} {\text{mol}}^{- 1}\right)}{\left(0 \cdot 0 8 \text{kg}\right)}$

= 1.506 mol kg-1 = 1.506 m

By rounding off to one place, we get the molality as 1.5 and by further multiplying it with 10, we get "15" as the final answer.

Density of this solution at 298 K is 2.0 g $\text{c}{\text{m}}^{- 3}$ . The ratio of the molecular weights of the solute and solvent, $\left(\dfrac{M{W}_{solute}}{M{W}_{solvent}}\right)$ , is
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{{X}_{solute}}{{X}_{solvent}} = \dfrac{0.1}{0.9} = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$\dfrac{{W}_{solute}}{{W}_{solvent}} \times \dfrac{{M}_{solvent}}{{M}_{solute}} = \dfrac{1}{9}$ ...(i)

${W}_{solute} + {W}_{solvent} = {W}_{solution} = density \times volume$

${W}_{solute} + {W}_{solvent} = 2 \times V$ ...(ii)

Molarity = molality

$\dfrac{{n}_{solute}}{{V}_{solution}} = \dfrac{{n}_{solute}}{{W}_{solvent}}$

${W}_{solvent} = {V}_{solution} = \dfrac{{W}_{solute} + {W}_{solvent}}{2}$

$2{W}_{solvent} = {W}_{solute} + {W}_{solvent}$

${W}_{solute} = {W}_{solvent}$ ...(iii)

Using equation (i) and (iii), we get

$\dfrac{{M}_{solute}}{{M}_{solvent}} = 9$

questions.solution:
Let atomic weight of element P is p and that of element Q is q.

For $P{Q}_{2}, n = \dfrac{w}{Mol. wt.}$

$0.1 = \dfrac{10}{p + 2q}$

$p + 2q = \dfrac{10}{0.1} = 100$...(i)

For ${P}_{3}{Q}_{2}, n = \dfrac{w}{Mol. wt.}$

$0.05 = \dfrac{9}{3p + 2q}$

$3p + 2q = \dfrac{9}{0.05} = 180$...(ii)

On solving equation (i) and (ii) we get q = 30

$p + 2 ( 30 ) = 100$

$p = 100 - 60 = 40$

questions.q: In an experiment, 2.4 g of iron oxide on reduction with hydrogen gave 1.68 g of iron. In another experiment, 2.9 g of iron oxide gave 2.09 g of iron on reduction. Which law is illustrated from the above data?
questions.solution:
In first experiment,

24 g of iron oxide gave 1.68 g of iron.

Mass of iron oxide $= 2.4$ g

Mass of iron $= 1.68$ g

Mass of oxygen $= 2.4 - 1.68 = 0.72$

Ratio of masses of iron and oxygen $= \dfrac{1.68}{0.72} = 7: 3$

In second experiment,

Mass of iron oxide $= 2.9$ g

Mass of iron $= 2.09$ g

Mass of oxygen $= 2.9 - 2.09 = 0.81$

Ratio of masses of iron and oxygen $= \dfrac{2.09}{0.81} = 7: 3$
